articles.title: Patricio Guzmán obituary
articles.summary: Chilean film-maker whose trilogy on Augusto Pinochet’s coup brought him to international attention. Hawker Hunter jets bomb the presidential palace in the Chilean capital, Santiago, setting it ablaze.
body: These are the dramatic opening images of the documentary film trilogy La Batalla de Chile (The Battle of Chile), directed by Patricio Guzmán. The three films detail the struggles of the Allende government to stay in power and promote what it termed “the peaceful road to socialism”. Filmed at the time with interviews, direct footage of demonstrations, debates about how to take the Allende government forward and opposition attacks that eventually led to Pinochet’s brutal seizure of power, it had a hard-hitting immediacy that brought Guzmán a huge audience and reputation outside Chile – although the three films remained banned for many years in his own country.

While he was filming during the September 1973 coup, Guzmán, who has died aged 85, was arrested and became one of the thousands of people taken to the Estadio Nacional football stadium in Santiago, where many were arbitrarily imprisoned and tortured. He was released after a fortnight and left the country in November, first going to Spain and then Cuba, before settling in Paris, where he lived for most of the rest of his life.

articles.title: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’
articles.summary: Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma. The singer shared the news on his Instagram on Tuesday, with the caption “A little health update” under the video. “Hey everybody.
body: Kelley likened sharing the news of his health with his sobriety journey: “Just getting this stuff off your chest is so freeing, and it takes the power away from it a little bit that we want to let y’all know what was going on. But we’re going to get through it. You know, I think in sobriety it’s all about one day at a time and that we’re not in control, and so that’s the way we’re looking at it.”

Kelley has been outspoken about his struggles with alcohol, and in 2022, the band — formerly known as Lady Antebellum — shared that they would be postponing the remainder of their “Request Line Tour” in support of Charles Kelley’s “journey to sobriety.”

The singer concluded the video by sharing that he is “hopeful” and will “try” to let fans in throughout the journey. “It’s just another hurdle, and you know, I’m confident that we’re going to get through it.”
From Dec. 10 through 21, the group will perform a run of Christmas shows as part of the “This Winter’s Night” tour.

articles.title: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing
articles.summary: HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday, Cindy Holland announced she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct to consumer streamers under the Paramount umbrella.
body: “As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here,” Holland wrote.

Over the past few weeks, speculation emerged that Bloys was likely to come over post merger in the top role overseeing all streaming operations. Bloys is a near 25-year veteran of HBO who has steered TV’s most prestigious brand through choppy waters and three massive corporate takeovers in eight years. There’s also speculation that JB Perrette, who now heads streaming business operations and gaming for WBD, will join Bloys in steering HBO, HBO Max and Paramount+.

articles.title: Penn Badgley Swore Off Sex Scenes. His Wife Says It Was Not Her Idea: ‘He Decided to Do This for Mental Health Reasons’
articles.summary: Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Feb. 2013 that he told showrunner Sera Gamble he was no longer interested in filming intimate scenes on camera.
body: “A few years ago, the internet decided I’d asked my husband to stop doing sex scenes. The truth is, my husband decided to do this for mental health reasons,” Kirke-Badgley wrote on Instagram. “After working in the industry since he was just 12 years old, believe me, it was time. In the entertainment world, they call actors ‘puppets’ behind their backs, and it’s even more disturbing when they start out as child actors… after years of trying, Penn decided to take a stand and let the world see him. And guess what, he hasn’t lost fans and he’s still getting hired!”

“The characters that my husband has played over the years, people have come to expect that he will continue to play that guy,” she added in the video post. “I was super happy for him and very proud of him because I understood how major it was, and yeah … it’s just relational hygiene.”
Badgley has been married since 2017 to Kirke-Badgley, who “encouraged” him to play Joe on “You” even though the part required him to film various sex scenes.

body: The big-scale family adventure project hails from Aton Soumache, the French producer behind Mark Osborne’s 2015 animated feature "The Little Prince" and the "Miraculous" franchise.

This new project will pull elements from French comic book artist and filmmaker Joann Sfar’s acclaimed graphic adaptation of “The Little Prince,” portraying the bond between the Little Prince and the Aviator.

The film will blend Saint-Exupéry’s real-life story as a pioneering aviator and writer with the fantastical world of “The Little Prince.” Saint-Exupéry’s story will unfold in live action, while the Little Prince will be created using visual effects.

“I see it as a very cinematic and epic story, one that gives us a wonderful opportunity to ask big questions,” Tyldum said. “This is a story about love, grief and loss. It’s about hope, following your heart’s desire and seeing life as a big adventure.”

articles.title: Digger review – Tom Cruise’s loudmouth oil tycoon goes hard in Alejandro G Iñárritu’s eco-satire
articles.summary: One man’s irresponsible drilling causes a global crisis in Iñárritu’s exasperatingly laborious, self-congratulatory film. A new movie from the Oscar-winning Mexican director Alejandro González Iñárritu is always an event.
body: An ageing, paunchy Texan oil tycoon called “Digger” Rockwell is seen fretfully getting up in the morning, cooing over his horrible old incontinent cat, taking urgent messages from underlings about a certain situation developing in his drilling station in the frozen Arctic. He is played by Tom Cruise with a wispy baldingness and various other prostheses, together with a good-ol’-boy twang and a Stetson borrowed from Slim Pickens’s bomb-riding army major in Kubrick’s Dr Strangelove. His prized possession is the battered old shovel his granddaddy used a century before, digging for black gold as a penniless young man in the lone star state. Digger likes to brandish this to make a point.

Digger’s – and the world’s – troubles come to a head when he is informed by his cringingly polite, querulous and terrified chief scientist Ganesh (Riz Ahmed) that the company’s irresponsible drilling practices, of which Ganesh has been warning Digger for quite some time, have caused a crisis: a vast ice floe, many times the size of Manhattan island, has broken away from the Arctic landmass and is now moving quickly towards the coast of Norway. Its imminent landfall is going to be like a nuclear attack.
points: One man’s irresponsible drilling causes a global crisis in Iñárritu’s exasperatingly laborious, self-congratulatory film.

articles.title: Close-up look at Turner's '£50m' Rome painting on show in the city
articles.summary: Turner’s early 19th century painting - Rome, from Mount Aventine - will be on display in the Italian capital for the first time ahead of an auction in London in December.
body: A renowned painting by British landscape artist JMW Turner has returned to the city that inspired it nearly two centuries ago.
Rome, from Mount Aventine features a panoramic view of the Italian capital and will be on display at the Palazzo Rondinini for three days.
Dating back to the 19th century, the masterpiece was based on sketches made in Rome.
The work of art is remarkably well preserved and is believed to have never been restored. It even features traces of fingerprints and brush hairs are still visible.

articles.title: The Portuguese House review – picturesque, polite drama of secrets and revelations at a country estate
articles.summary: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener. Out of the blue, a woman walks out on her husband.
body: Manolo Solo gives an excellent performance as the left-behind husband, Fernando, an introspective mild-mannered geography professor. After his wife’s disappearance, Fernando goes on holiday to Portugal, where he meets a gardener called Manuel. When Manuel drops dead of a heart attack, Fernando decides – like his wife – to leave his old life behind; he assumes Manuel’s identity and takes a job as the gardener at a Portuguese country estate. The owner, Amália (Maria de Medeiros), senses that this intellectual man with glasses and a clumsy way with the loppers is not the man she hired, but doesn’t push it – possibly because she is attracted to him.

Like a doorstop paperback, The Portuguese House is an expansive watch, spanning years and going at a gentle pace for nearly two hours. There are more secrets and lies to come – and another person pretending to be someone they are not. That would be a twist too far in another film, but works here in a restrained drama that treats all its characters generously and with sympathy. Though in the end I wondered if it is possibly too respectful, sweeping away difficult hard-to-shift feelings like autumn leaves.
points: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener.

articles.summary: In collaboration with Frances Valentine, the 20-piece drop includes clothing and accessories, with a portion of the profits going to help people living with the chronic condition.
body: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Frances Valentine, the fashion brand created by the late Kate Spade and her friend Elyce Arons, is dipping into the glamorous world of old Hollywood with a new Mary Tyler Moore collection that pays homage to the actress.

The limited-edition capsule features 19 pieces, including shirts, dresses, tote bags and, of course, shoes, all inspired by the Emmy-winning star’s whimsical, upscale style. Prices start at $48 for a makeup clutch and go up to $498 for wool peacoats.
The actress was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes in the Sixties, at age 33, just as she was entering one of the most successful periods of her career.

articles.title: Sir Ranulph Fiennes' relatives tell BBC it's 'very painful' not being able to visit him
articles.summary: It has been alleged that Sir Ranulph has been admitted to a number of care homes under assumed names.
body: Relatives of the British explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes have said it is "very painful" he appears to have been hidden away from them.
Speaking to BBC Newsnight, his former sister-in-law told the BBC that she did not know where he was, and nobody had been able to see him.
Louise Millington-Cotes did not immediately respond to the allegations, or the BBC's request for comment.
Cheshire Police have said they are aware of the concerns regarding Sir Ranulph, and are satisfied he is living in an appropriate setting with suitable care.
